classification.difficultyReason: Recognise odd or even symmetry, determine the sign on half the interval and evaluate a polynomial integral to obtain positive area.

content.prompt:
Look carefully for any symmetries that will simplify the calculation.
Find the area of the region bounded by the given curve and the $x$-axis.

answer.worked:
$y=x^7$ is odd, so the areas on $[-2,0]$ and $[0,2]$ are equal. On $[0,2]$, the curve is above the $x$-axis.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=2\int_0^2x^7\,dx\\&=2\left[\frac{x^8}{8}\right]_0^2\\&=2\left(\frac{256}{8}-0\right)\\&=64\text{ units}^2\end{aligned}$$

The function is odd, so its graph is symmetric about the origin. Its zeros are $x=-4,0,4$.
On $[0,4]$, $x(x-4)(x+4)\le0$. For example, at $x=2$, $y=2(-2)(6)=-24$, below the $x$-axis.
By symmetry,
$$A=2\left(-\int_0^4(x^3-16x)\,dx\right).$$
$$\begin{aligned}\int_0^4(x^3-16x)\,dx&=\left[\frac{x^4}{4}-8x^2\right]_0^4\\&=(64-128)-0\\&=-64\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}A&=2(64)\\&=128\text{ units}^2\end{aligned}$$

The function is even, so its graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis. Its zeros are $x=-3,0,3$.
On $[0,3]$, the curve is on or below the $x$-axis. For example, at $x=1$, $y=1-9=-8$.
By symmetry,
$$A=2\left(-\int_0^3(x^4-9x^2)\,dx\right).$$
$$\begin{aligned}\int_0^3(x^4-9x^2)\,dx&=\left[\frac{x^5}{5}-3x^3\right]_0^3\\&=\left(\frac{243}{5}-81\right)-0\\&=-\frac{162}{5}\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}A&=2\left(\frac{162}{5}\right)\\&=\frac{324}{5}\\&=64\frac45\text{ units}^2\end{aligned}$$
